question: The summer 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey, starring Matt Damon, follows a Greek king's long voyage home. Which war is he sailing home from?
source_excerpt: Matt Damon will be playing titular king Odysseus.

extra.why_interesting: Players know the film was a huge summer release but may not have thought about where the story starts. Most can reach the answer from half-remembered school myths: the wooden horse, Helen, Achilles.

topicality.rationale: Hooks a classic-myth answer to Nolan's big summer 2026 release, which stays in conversation for a season.

extra.verification_notes: Nolan's The Odyssey (released July 17, 2026) stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, king of Ithaca, who sails home from the Trojan War.

explanation: Odysseus thought up the wooden horse that ended the Trojan War. The gods then punished him with ten more years at sea before he reached Ithaca.

question: In summer 2026, one young actor played Odysseus's son Telemachus in The Odyssey and also headlined a rival superhero blockbuster released just two weeks later. Who is he?

extra.why_interesting: The two biggest films of summer 2026 were treated as box-office rivals. Many players never noticed they shared a lead actor, playing a Greek prince in one and a superhero in the other.

topicality.rationale: Depends on Tom Holland's summer 2026 double release, a blockbuster-season talking point.

extra.verification_notes: Tom Holland plays Telemachus in The Odyssey (July 17, 2026) and stars in Spider-Man: Brand New Day (July 31, 2026), per cast lists such as https://www.capitalxtra.com/news/the-odyssey-2026-cast-release-date/.

explanation: Tom Holland went straight from ancient Greece to swinging through New York in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. That summer he was effectively competing with himself at the box office.

question: A new Resident Evil film hit cinemas in September 2026, but in Japan, where the games are made, the series has a different English name. What is it, a hint at its zombie-making viruses?
source_excerpt: Resident Evil ... theatrically released in the United States on September 18, 2026, by Sony Pictures Releasing

extra.why_interesting: Players assume the franchise has the same name everywhere. Its home country actually uses a blunter, one-word English title that players can work out from the series' viruses and outbreaks.

topicality.rationale: Framed around the September 2026 Resident Evil film release, though the Biohazard fact itself is evergreen.

extra.verification_notes: The film released September 18, 2026 in the US, and the Japanese series title is 'Biohazard' (English word); only the Japan opening (reportedly October 9) differs, which the question doesn't claim.

explanation: In Japan it has always been Biohazard. The name was changed for the West partly because a rock band and other products already used it.

question: In 1992 Queen's Bohemian Rhapsody suddenly returned to the charts, after a film scene of friends in a small car headbanging along to it. Which comedy film?
source_excerpt: The song returned to the US chart 17 years later after its use in the 1992 film Wayne's World.

extra.why_interesting: People assume the song's lasting fame is down to Freddie Mercury alone. In fact, a silly car scene in a comedy film introduced it to a whole new generation in America. It also suits a question heard in the car.

topicality.rationale: 1992 film and music trivia with no current news hook.

extra.verification_notes: Wayne's World (1992) car headbanging scene revived Bohemian Rhapsody, which hit No. 2 on the Hot 100 in 1992; no newer event changes this (https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/waynes-world-gave-queen-a-us-hit/).

explanation: Mike Myers and friends headbanging in a battered AMC Pacer sent the song to number two in the US. That was higher than it had reached there on its first release.

question: In Squid Game, the giant doll's deadly game is known worldwide as Red Light, Green Light. But in Korean the doll actually sings that a certain flower has bloomed. Which flower, South Korea's national flower?
source_excerpt: Mugunghwa flower is Korea's national flower; in English, it's known as the 'Rose of Sharon'.

extra.why_interesting: Worldwide audiences know the game as 'Red Light, Green Light' and assume the doll is saying something like it. In fact, the eerie chant is about a flower blooming, and the stem's hint about the national flower gives players a way to reason it out.

topicality.rationale: General Korean culture trivia about a 2021 show, not fresh news.

extra.verification_notes: The doll sings that the mugunghwa (rose of Sharon, Hibiscus syriacus) has bloomed; it is Korea's national flower, so 'Hibiscus' is acceptable though 'Rose of Sharon' is the common name.

explanation: She sings that the mugunghwa, the hibiscus also called rose of Sharon, has bloomed. She turns around on the last word, just like Korean children do in the playground version.

question: Mario is the world's most famous plumber, but in his very first game, Donkey Kong, climbing girders on a building site, he had a different job. What was it?
source_excerpt: Mario was originally a carpenter in Donkey Kong; he became a plumber in Mario Bros. because the underground settings suited a plumber.

extra.why_interesting: Mario the plumber is one of the most fixed identities in pop culture, so it surprises players that he started out in a different trade. The construction-site girders of Donkey Kong give a fair foothold to work it out.
extra.verification_notes: Mario (Jumpman) was a carpenter in Donkey Kong (1981) and became a plumber in Mario Bros. (1983); no newer development changes this (Wikipedia, List of Mario franchise characters).

explanation: Nintendo made him a carpenter to suit the construction-site setting. He only took up plumbing a couple of years later, when Mario Bros. sent him down into the sewers.

question: Everyone quotes Darth Vader as saying 'Luke, I am your father', but that is not what he says in The Empire Strikes Back. What is the actual first word of that famous line?
source_excerpt: No, Darth Vader does not say "Luke, I am your father." The actual line is "No, I am your father."

extra.why_interesting: Nearly everyone 'remembers' the line with Luke's name in it. Realising that the real first word is a reply to Luke's accusation feels like a small Mandela-effect jolt, and anyone who replays the scene in their head can reason their way there.

topicality.rationale: Classic film misquote trivia from 1980; not news.

extra.verification_notes: Vader's actual line is 'No, I am your father', so the first word 'No' is correct; the 'Luke,' version is a well-known misquote (https://www.weareiowa.com/article/news/verify/star-wars-day-darth-vader-luke-father-line-misquoted/536-c6a3fcd3-41ce-4a50-b2ea-6a28b342a86d).

explanation: Luke has just accused Vader of killing his father, so Vader answers 'No, I am your father.' Luke's name never appears in the line.
